body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending. Claims 1-19 are amended. No new matter has been added.
Claim Rejection - 35 USC § 101

Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §101 because the claimed invention is directed to a judicial exception (i.e., a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea) without significantly more. This rejection is respectfully traversed.
It is stated on page 3 of the office action that "[a] human appears capable of

performing the process steps underlined in claim 1. A human can: access a profile model that is used to generate predictive indicators, receive a request for accessing a game, and generate assistance input for the user responsive to the predictive indicators, such that the assistance input is provided before the user performs the task". As per MPEP section §2103, "[t]he claimed invention as a whole must be useful". Claim 1 does not just recite "access a profile model that is used to generate predictive indicators" but recites "accessing an artificial intelligence model via a user account of a user, wherein the artificial intelligence model is used to generate one or more predictive indicators based on a plurality of game contexts during a plurality of game sessions of one or more games, wherein the one or more predictive indicators identify that the user will be unable to complete the task during a game". Also, claim 1 does not just recite "receive a request for accessing a game" but recites "receiving a request for accessing the game for the game session via the user account". As such, it is
respectfully submitted that claim 1, as a whole, must be useful.
It is respectfully submitted that claim 1 is not directed to abstract idea. Rather, claim

1 is directed to "a method for providing assistance to a hand-held controller during gameplay". Claim 1 includes "accessing an artificial intelligence model via a user account of a user, wherein the artificial intelligence model is used to generate one or more predictive indicators based on a plurality of game contexts during a plurality of game sessions of one or more games, wherein the one or more predictive indicators identify that the user will be unable to complete a task during a game". The artificial intelligence model cannot be accessed mentally. For example, a user's brain cannot receive the artificial intelligence model. Also, the user cannot mentally receive "a request for accessing the game for a game

session via the user account". The user's brain is not coupled to the user account to mentally receive the request. Moreover, the user cannot mentally provide the "assistance input via a computer network to the hand-held controller operated by the user during the game context responsive to the one or more predictive indicators that the user will be unable to complete the task in the game context". Therefore, claim 1 is not directed to an abstract idea.

Even if one were to argue that claim 1 is directed to an abstract idea, the abstract idea is integrated into a practical application. The practical application includes accessing an artificial intelligence model to generate one or more predictive indicators to identify that the user will be unable to complete a task during a game session and provide assistance input via a computer network to a hand-held controller during a game context of the game session. The game context is similar to one or more game contexts used to generate the one or more predictive indicators. By providing the assistance input to the hand-held controller via the computer network, the user can complete the task in the game. As such, claim 1 recites the practical application. Therefore, it is respectfully submitted that claim 1 is directed to statutory subject matter and is useful.
Also, for the same reasons set forth above, independent claims 8 and 15 are submitted to be useful.

Claims 2-7 depend from independent claim 1, claims 9-14 depend from independent claim 8, and claims 16-20 depend from independent claim 15. For the same reasons set forth above with respect to the independent claims 1, 8, and 15, the respective dependent claims 2- 7, 9-14, and 16-20 are submitted to be useful.
Hence, for the reason set forth above, it is respectfully requested that the section 101 rejection of claims 1-20 be withdrawn.
Claim Rejection - 35 USC § 112
Claims 7 & 14 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) or 35 U.S.C. §112 (pre-AIA),

second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre- AIA 35 U.S.C. §112, the applicant), regards as the invention. This rejection is respectfully traversed. Claims 7 and 14 have been amended. As such, and it is respectfully requested that the section 112 rejection of claims 7 and 14 be withdrawn.
Claim Rejection - 35 USC § 102

Claims 1-5, 7-12, & 14-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Osman et al. (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0001205; hereinafter "Osman"). This rejection is respectfully traversed.

It has not been shown that Osman discloses "accessing an artificial intelligence model via a user account of a user, wherein the artificial intelligence model is used to generate one or more predictive indicators based on a plurality of game contexts during a plurality of game sessions of one or more games, wherein the one or more predictive indicators identify that the user will be unable to complete a task during a game; .. determining that the game session includes a game context similar to one or more of the plurality of game contexts", as is recited in claim 1. As stated in Figure 3A, in an operation 320, a plurality of gameplays of a user are monitored and in an operation 340, an instance of a gaming application is controlled based on a game

play style of the user. As such, it has not been shown that an AI of Osman "is used to generate one or more predictive indicators based on a plurality of game contexts during a plurality of game sessions of one or more games" to "identify that the user will be unable to complete a task during a game".

Osman further describes in paragraph 19 that "the game play controller is able to play the game for the user to complete difficult tasks. For example, when the user is stuck (e.g., how to open the green door?) the user is able to query the gaming system for help". It is further described in paragraph 4 of Osman that "the AI character can proceed in automatic mode to complete specific game tasks that are difficult for the user". However, it has not been shown that the AI character of Osman "is used to generate one or more predictive indicators based on a plurality of game contexts during a plurality of game sessions of one or more games" to "identify that the user will be unable to complete a task during a game". Hence, claim 1 is submitted to be novel.

Also, for the same reasons set forth above, the independent claims 8 and 15 are submitted to be novel. For example, it has all been shown that Osman discloses a processor configured to "access an artificial intelligence model via a user account of a user, wherein the artificial intelligence model is used to generate one or more predictive indicators based on a plurality of game contexts during a plurality of game sessions of one or more games, wherein the one or more predictive indicators identify that the user will be unable to complete a task during a game; . . . determine that the game session includes a game context similar to one or more of the plurality of game contexts", as is recited in claim 8. As another example, it is not been shown that Osman discloses a server configured to "access an artificial intelligence model via a user account of a user, wherein the artificial intelligence model is used to generate one or more predictive indicators based on a plurality of game contexts during a plurality of game sessions of one or more games, wherein the one or more predictive indicators identify that the user will be unable to complete a task during a game; . determine that the game session includes a game context similar to one or more of the plurality of game contexts", as is recited in claim 15.
Claims 2-5 and 7 depend from independent claim 1, claims 9-12 and 14 depend from independent claim 8, and claims 16-20 depend from independent claim 15. For the same
reasons set forth above with respect to the independent claims 1, 8, and 15, the respective dependent claims 2-5, 7, 9-12, 14, and 16-20 are submitted to be novel.
Hence, for the reasons set forth above, it is respectfully requested that the section 102 rejection of claims 1-5, 7-12, & 14-20 be withdrawn.
A Notice of Allowance is respectfully requested.
